topics.title: The channel, resources and information quantities
topics.introduction:
The receiver can distinguish intact transmission from destructive measurement. In the measured branch it receives an axis label and a noisy sign. The distinction between accessible records and hidden outcomes fixes the channel whose capacity is studied.

The definitions below specify the operation budget before introducing the information quantities. The same reporting error applies to every axis and every use; this assumption is used later in the scalar entropy comparison. [The physical picture](physical-picture.md) gives a gentler explanation, and [the notation crosswalk](notation.md) connects the proof to its sources and implementations.
topics.continuation: With the channel fixed, [the global one-use criterion](single-use.md) determines exactly when its optimized coherent information becomes zero.

topics.title: The exact one-use boundary and the repetition frontier
topics.introduction:
The comparison begins with every single-qubit density matrix, including mixed inputs arbitrarily close to purity. Conditioning on the reported records gives an exact coherent-information identity and a global minimization problem.

The one-use positivity boundary is exact. The repetition frontier refers to a specified family of sufficiently long balanced blocks; [its coding proof](repetition-coding.md) establishes that separate statement. The nearly pure directional cost supplies an upper bound on the global minimum. [The mixed-input control](eight-use-witness.md#p134) explains why it cannot generally be substituted for that minimum.
topics.continuation: The next step is to bound the global cost for every input. [Entropy tools and the endpoint chord](entropy-tools.md) provide the reduction used by the scalar inequality.

topics.title: Entropy tools and the common-error comparison
topics.introduction:
Two parts of the proof use the same conditional-state entropies in different ways. The one-use argument compares costs over all input eigenvalues and directions; the repetition argument bounds the entropy carried by complete classical records.

The elementary tools are stated first. An integral representation then reveals two compatible curvature properties in different variables. Its endpoint chord has one coefficient shared by all axes because their reporting error is common. [The scalar inequality](scalar-inequality.md) bounds the remaining intercept uniformly.
topics.continuation: Use [the scalar lemma and its complete domain coverage](scalar-inequality.md) for the global one-use obstruction. The overlap bounds return in [the all-record repetition construction](repetition-coding.md#p09).

topics.title: The scalar entropy inequality and its certificate
topics.introduction:
The geometric theorem needs an entropy comparison valid throughout the open reporting-error interval and for every input eigenvalue. This page gives the full scalar statement and its proof obligations.

Analytical arguments cover regions approaching both noise endpoints and arbitrarily nearly pure inputs. The remaining compact domain is covered by an exact rational certificate, checked by three separate arithmetic implementations. The computational intervals enclose complete regions; the result is not inferred from a grid of sampled channels. [Verification commands and expected outputs](../verification/README.md) explain how to inspect the evidence.
topics.continuation: With the scalar inequality established, [the geometric argument](geometric-gap.md#p08) separates the global one-use cost from the repetition loss.

topics.title: Full-span separation and universal linear closure
topics.introduction:
The smallest frame eigenvalue measures the least weighted squared projection onto a possible plane normal. Full span makes this quantity positive and removes a common perpendicular direction. The argument below turns that geometric fact into a strict separation between two entropy costs.

The theorem states the quantifiers and the conservative sufficient interval. The corollary then gives two-sided linear bounds on the gap between the exact one-use boundary and the balanced-repetition frontier, uniformly over finite ensembles at each fixed interior error. A threshold width does not determine a communication rate or a uniform block length. Capacity positivity also uses [the finite-block and outer-coding argument](repetition-coding.md#p10).
topics.continuation: [Repetition coding](repetition-coding.md) supplies the positive finite block required by the theorem. [Limiting geometries](limiting-geometries.md) gives the restricted coplanar converse and an exactly soluble cone family.

topics.title: All-record repetition coding and positive capacity
topics.introduction:
A fixed isometry encodes a logical qubit into the span of two antipodal product codewords. The balanced average input is separable but correlated, while its purification retains the logical coherence relevant to quantum transmission.

Every mask and reported record contributes to the coherent information, including the negative all-measured term. Polynomial prefactors and competing exponential bases determine the strict eventual sign. A positive finite inner block is selected before taking the separate asymptotic outer-coding limit. This order does not require the inner-block rate to have a positive limit as its length grows.
topics.continuation: [The eight-use witness](eight-use-witness.md) evaluates one explicit positive block. [The limiting cases](limiting-geometries.md) delimit what the repetition argument establishes.

topics.title: Coplanarity, noise endpoints and the exact cone family
topics.introduction:
The boundary cases clarify the content of the full-span guarantee. Coplanarity closes the strict comparison for long balanced repetitions, while the two noise endpoints follow from direct channel arguments. The coplanar statement is scoped to that coding comparison.

The universal closure result controls every allowed sequence of weighted ensembles at a fixed interior error. The cone family supplies a particular exact leading coefficient and has its own stated validity domain. Small frame eigenvalue can arise from small weights on out-of-plane axes as well as from axes moving toward a plane.
topics.continuation: The Pauli witness uses a sharper equality case within the valid cone domain. See [its complete calculation and numerical controls](eight-use-witness.md).

topics.title: The eight-use witness and numerical controls
topics.introduction:
This example makes the theorem's coding interpretation concrete. A global bound proves that every one-use input has nonpositive coherent information, while a directed arithmetic enclosure certifies a positive value for one balanced eight-use block.

The calculation includes all measured-count classes and the loss when all qubits are measured. Its per-use value becomes an achievable rate through outer coding; it does not specify recovery fidelity for an isolated block. The accompanying mixed-input and cancellation controls guard against two tempting but invalid shortcuts. [Figure 1](../reader/figures.md#figure-1) presents the same retained numerical inputs.
topics.continuation: [The proof and evidence map](proof-map.md) connects this witness, the general theorem and the limiting cases to their exact dependencies and source records.
